files: Static AST helper, run in a child interpreter. Reads one request on stdin and writes one JSON response on stdout. It parses the target source to a syntax tree and does not import or execute it (claim `helper-source-has-no-execution-primitives`, checked on the helper source text).
Entry points analyzePythonFile and analyzePythonFiles, interpreter discovery, request and response envelopes.
Project facts from helper results: module identity, import resolution, symbol resolution.
Annotation normalization into type facts for model fields.
Pydantic, SQLModel and settings model facts from class facts.
Shadow FastAPI endpoints, mounts, entities and DTOs, and the parity report against a legacy scan.
Shadow Flask route registrations and declarations.
Shadow Django URL registrations and includes composed from urlpatterns.

batch result.what: Return value of analyzePythonFiles: ok is true only when every result is ok; runtime is null when no interpreter was needed or found.

file result ok.what: Successful result for one file: the facts, the interpreter identity and the source encoding.

file result failure.what: Failed result for one file: ok false with an error and the source reference. An analysis failure is returned in this shape and not thrown; a file-system error raised while the source is resolved or read is thrown as it is.

error.what: An error without position: a code from the code table and a message.

error with position.what: A syntax error: code, message and the span reported by the interpreter parser.

source reference.what: The bytes a result describes. sha256 is absent for oversize files and encoding is present only on success.

helper runtime.what: Interpreter identity inside a successful file result: implementation and version as a list of integers.

runtime handle.what: Interpreter found by discovery: realpath of the executable and version as text; also the runtime of a batch.

facts.what: The seven fact lists the helper extracts from top-level statements.

import fact.what: One import statement at the top level.

imported name.what: One imported name of an import fact, with its alias.

assignment fact.what: A top-level or class-body assignment: targets, optional annotation, value.

augmented assignment fact.what: A top-level augmented assignment; operator is the Python operator class name and is not a closed set.

call statement fact.what: A top-level or class-body expression statement that is a call.

control-flow mutation assignment.what: An assignment nested in control flow, recorded only as a mutation fact.

control-flow mutation augmented-assignme.what: An augmented assignment nested in control flow, recorded only as a mutation fact.

control-flow mutation call.what: A call statement nested in control flow, recorded only as a mutation fact.

function fact.what: A top-level function or a method.

class fact.what: A top-level class with its bases, keywords, decorators, fields, methods and call statements.

class keyword.what: One keyword in a class header, for example metaclass or table.

call keyword.what: One keyword argument of a call value.

mapping entry.what: One key and value of a mapping value.

value constant.what: A string, boolean, None or a number inside the JavaScript safe range.

value integer.what: An integer outside the JavaScript safe range, kept as decimal text with a reason.

value float-special.what: A non-finite float kept as text with a reason.

value unknown.what: An expression the helper does not evaluate; node is the Python AST class name.

value missing.what: No expression was present (for example an absent annotation or default).

value symbol.what: A name or dotted attribute chain.

value sequence.what: A list, tuple or set display with its items.

value mapping.what: A dict display with its entries.

value call.what: A call with callee, arguments and keywords.

value subscript.what: A subscript with base and slice.

value binary.what: A binary operation; only the BitOr operator is recorded, any other operator is an unknown value.

project.what: Return value of buildPythonProjectFacts: the analyzed modules, the collisions and the lookups used by the other modules.

module entry.what: One analyzed module: identity, source, facts and the resolution of each of its imports.

collision.what: Several sources that map to one module id. Every source of a collision is excluded from the project.

import resolution module.what: Resolution of a plain import of a module.

import resolution symbol.what: Resolution of a from-import of one name.

import resolution ambiguous-import.what: An import whose target module id is a collision.

resolution resolved.what: A symbol resolved to a module and an optional name. The name is not checked for existence.

resolution unknown with locality.what: No resolution, but the locality of the module is known.

resolution unknown bare.what: No resolution and nothing else is known.

resolution unknown value.what: resolveValueSymbol was given a value that is not a symbol.

resolution cyclic-symbol-alias.what: Following re-exports returned to a symbol already visited.

resolution ambiguous-module.what: The symbol leads into a module id that is a collision.

resolution ambiguous-import-target.what: A name could be a submodule or a symbol of a package; both exist, so nothing is chosen.

type unknown.what: The annotation could not be normalized; reason says why and raw keeps the fact when there is one.

type forward-reference.what: A string annotation, kept as text and not parsed.

type reference.what: A name that resolved to a module and an optional name.

type unresolved-reference.what: A name that did not resolve; reason carries the resolver reason or unresolved.

type union.what: A union written as pep604, typing.Optional or typing.Union (syntax says which).

type annotated.what: typing.Annotated: the base type and the metadata value facts.

type generic.what: A subscripted type: base and arguments.

model.what: A class with a pydantic, SQLModel or settings ancestor. Classes of an unknown family are omitted.

model bases.what: Bases of a model split into local models (as refs) and external dotted names.

model field.what: A field of a model, declared in the class body.

field metadata.what: Keyword facts read from a pydantic or sqlmodel Field call.

annotated model field.what: A model field after annotatePythonModelTypes, with its typeFact.

fastapi endpoint.what: A route declared with a literal path on a locally declared APIRouter.

fastapi mount.what: An include_router call on a locally declared app or router. Mounts are recorded, not composed.

mount child resolved.what: The router argument of a mount resolved to a module and a name.

mount child unknown.what: The router argument of a mount could not be resolved.

fastapi entity.what: A SQLModel class with table=True and its primary key fields.

parity counts.what: Counts of the legacy summary and of the shadow.

parity side counts.what: Endpoint, entity and DTO counts of one side.

parity difference.what: Keys present on one side only, for endpoints, entities or DTOs.

flask registration.what: A route decorator with a literal rule on a locally declared app or blueprint.

flask declaration.what: A locally declared Flask app or Blueprint with its prefix status.

django registration.what: A path or re_path entry composed with the include prefixes above it.

django include.what: An include edge from one url module to a child module (childModule is null when the target is not a literal module).

pattern segment.what: One pattern text with its kind (path or regex).

view target symbol.what: A view given as a name that resolved to a symbol.

view target class-view.what: A view given as Name.as_view(); the factory is recorded.

items.INVALID_REQUEST: Helper only: the request envelope could not be read. The analyzer always sends a valid one, so this code is unreachable through the entry points.
items.PYTHON_ANALYZER_FAILED: The helper did not complete: a spawn error other than a timeout (for example ENOBUFS when stdout passes maxBuffer), a non-zero exit (the message carries the first 800 characters of stderr) or an uncaught helper exception.
items.PYTHON_ANALYZER_PROTOCOL_ERROR: The helper exited 0 but stdout was not JSON, or the JSON lacked the response protocol or a boolean ok.
items.PYTHON_ANALYZER_TIMEOUT: The helper was killed after timeoutMs milliseconds.
items.PYTHON_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE: No approved interpreter was found. The result keeps path, sha256 and sizeBytes and has no facts.
items.PYTHON_SOURCE_ENCODING_UNSUPPORTED: The source declares an encoding the interpreter does not know, or its bytes do not decode.
items.PYTHON_SOURCE_TOO_LARGE: The file is larger than maxSourceBytes. Reported before any interpreter lookup; only path and sizeBytes are known.
items.PYTHON_SYNTAX_ERROR: The interpreter parser rejected the source. The error carries line, column, end_line and end_column.

items.pydantic: A base resolves to pydantic.BaseModel and no other family was found.
items.unknown: Internal: the class has no known family. Such classes are omitted from the output, so this word never appears in a result.

claims: An out-of-range timeoutMs, maxBuffer, maxSourceBytes or maxFiles throws the message in the options table even when the file does not exist.

Bad arguments, an over-long list, an empty entry, a duplicate after realpath, a path outside the root and a non-regular file throw the messages in the errors table; a missing file throws the raw ENOENT error and a file that cannot be read throws the raw EACCES error. This claim tries the missing file; the EACCES case is tried by a separate test that runs for an ordinary user and is reported as skipped, with a reason, where the process can read a file of mode 000 (root, for example).
A file larger than maxSourceBytes yields PYTHON_SOURCE_TOO_LARGE with only path and sizeBytes, and no interpreter is looked up.
Without an approved interpreter a file yields PYTHON_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE with path, sha256 (the digest of the file bytes) and sizeBytes and no facts.
An empty file list returns ok true and a null runtime; a batch of only oversize files returns ok false and a null runtime; neither looks for an interpreter.
An explicit pythonCommand that cannot be used yields no runtime; python3 and python are not tried.
Batch results are ordered by localeCompare of source.path, whatever the input order.
A symlink inside the root reports the path of its target; a symlink to a file outside the root throws.
BSKEL_PYTHON is tried first; a bare name is searched only in absolute PATH entries; versions below 3.8 and unparsable probe output are refused; an interpreter inside the project root is refused.
A timeout, a non-zero exit, output that is not JSON, a wrong envelope and an output flood are returned as ok false results with their codes.
The stderr text in a non-zero exit message is cut at 800 characters without a marker.
The helper gets -I -S -B -X utf8 and its own path as arguments, the request on stdin (protocol, filename, source_base64) and an environment without the variables of the parent process.

The helper source imports only ast, base64, io, json, math, sys and tokenize and contains no call of exec, eval, compile, open, __import__, and no use of os, subprocess, importlib or socket; among the JavaScript modules only analyzer.mjs imports node:child_process and node:fs, and it uses only statSync, realpathSync and readFileSync of the file system module.
The request and response constants of the helper equal the analyzer constants, and all three protocol strings end with /1.
No .mjs, .js, .cjs or .ts file under scanners/ outside this directory contains the text language/python; folders named node_modules are skipped.

An integer beyond plus or minus 2 to the power 53 minus 1 keeps its decimal text, an infinite float is float-special, a value is read down to its 13th nesting level and a node on the 14th level is unknown with reason depth-limit, and an operator other than BitOr is an unknown BinOp.

Functions, classes and imports inside control flow, nested functions, inner classes and assignments inside an if in a class body produce no fact; only assignments, augmented assignments and calls inside control flow are kept, as mutation facts.

A syntax error is a failed file with line, column, end_line and end_column; the two end fields are null when the interpreter reports no end position (before Python 3.10). An unknown or undecodable encoding is PYTHON_SOURCE_ENCODING_UNSUPPORTED.
Source with 300 nested parentheses is a failed file, not facts.
A chain of 20000 attributes makes the helper exit with a traceback, which is returned as PYTHON_ANALYZER_FAILED.
A match statement is read when the interpreter is Python 3.10 or newer and is a PYTHON_SYNTAX_ERROR on older interpreters.

The module id table equals the resolver output: extension removed, dots for separators, hyphens kept, a trailing __init__ removed, no source roots; the package id is the directory of the file written with dots.
A module and a package of the same id, or a module and its stub, produce a collision, no module entry, and locality ambiguous.
A result that is not ok is not in the project; its module id reads as external, and a name imported from it resolves as a name of an external module, not as unknown.
A dotted name under a resolved module or class is reported as resolved without checking that it exists.

Two classes of one name in a module give one model, the later one; two imports of one alias resolve to the later import. An assignment, a function or a class whose name is also an import alias does not replace the import, in either order: the alias is looked up before the names the module declares (not modeled).

A class is left out of the models, without a diagnostic, when none of its bases establishes a recognized family. A base that does not resolve is ignored: next to a base that establishes a family the class stays a model.
An aliased import of APIRouter is recognized; a local class named APIRouter is not.
The decorators options and api_route, and include_router on a receiver that is not a locally declared app or router, produce neither a fact nor a diagnostic.
The parity flag is true only when the difference count is zero and the shadow has no unknowns; differences are named by the keys of the identity table.

An include_router call is listed in mounts and in unknowns with the reason include-router-mount-not-composed; its prefix is not added to the endpoint paths, which carry only the prefix of their own router.

A register_blueprint call with a url_prefix leaves the result of the Flask shadow unchanged: no mount is recorded, a blueprint route keeps the prefix of its own blueprint, and its limitations list says that mount overrides are not composed.
add_url_rule, a bare route decorator and the options decorator produce neither a registration nor a diagnostic.
An include of a project module that has no urlpatterns is recorded as an include edge and produces no registration and no diagnostic.

A path, prefix, method list or URL pattern that is not a literal yields a diagnostic with a reason and no registration for that entry, and the literal registrations beside it are still reported (FastAPI, Flask and Django).
Project, model, type and shadow outputs carry no schema, protocol, version or id key.
limits: Module ids are the repository path with dots; a source root such as src is part of the id.
A file that fails to analyze disappears from the project and reads as an external module; a name imported from it resolves as external instead of unknown.
A name under a resolved module is not checked for existence.
Definitions and imports below the top level or inside control flow are not facts.
Some registrations are dropped without a diagnostic (listed in the FastAPI, Flask and Django claims).
A class none of whose bases establishes a recognized family is absent from the models; an unresolved base next to a recognized one is ignored and the class stays a model.
Two classes of one name and two imports of one alias keep only the last one. An assignment, a function or a class of an import alias name does not replace the import, in either order (not modeled).
A very long attribute chain fails the helper; where exactly depends on the interpreter, the claim uses 20000.
A reported FastAPI endpoint path is not the served URL: include_router prefixes are listed in mounts and are not added to endpoint paths.
A Flask register_blueprint call is not recorded and its url_prefix is ignored: a reported blueprint route path is the path under the prefix of its own blueprint, not necessarily the served URL.
The syntax accepted is the syntax of the interpreter that runs the helper, so a file can be readable on one host and a syntax error on another.
The batch order uses localeCompare, so it can differ between host locales.
The helper runs with the privileges of the caller; isolation is the -I -S -B flags, an empty environment and the absence of execution primitives, not a sandbox.
The memory used by the interpreter is not bounded by the layer.

The tables that the test recomputes come from small fixtures written in the test, not from real projects. Real projects are read by the corpus test of test/language-python/baseline-record.test.mjs, which fetches the pinned commits when BASELINE_CORPUS_FETCH is 1 and is skipped otherwise.
The samples hand-feed the legacy scan shape; the real legacy scanner is compared in test/language-python/python-fastapi-shadow.test.mjs.

The samples are recomputed on the interpreter that the test finds. The tables were checked to be identical on four local interpreters (versions 3.9, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.14); other versions and the CI interpreters are not recorded here.
Only the listed consumers are checked; an unlisted importer in another track is not detected.
Child-process checks use shell-script stand-ins and are not evaluated on win32.
The Windows branches of the interpreter search (executable extensions from PATHEXT, SystemRoot and WINDIR in the child environment) are read from the source and have not been run.

A word that the code builds by concatenation, such as the urlpatterns reasons, is checked through the samples and not through the source text, so a new variant of it is found only when a sample reaches it.
obligations: Minimal next or shadow implementation that preserves the stable path.
Any wiring of this layer into the stable scanner path.
Negative, mutation, permission and cross-version tests.
A claim that unknown or partial results are covered beyond the samples of this document.
Consumers, runner, provider and packed-artifact integration.
